title: Backup/restore fuzz-testing and progressive integrity assertions for passive DR
creator: Maya Lerner
description: Goal: Build and validate a repeatable fuzz-testing harness for snapshot/backup files and a progressive restore workflow that asserts data and KV-store integrity at each stage. This ticket covers design and implementation of: (1) a snapshot fuzz generator that mutates stored backups to surface restore failure modes, (2) progressive-restore safety-net logic that validates consistency after partial restores and can auto-abort, (3) SLO/telemetry gates and circuit-breaker integrations to ensure failing restores do not cascade into serving lanes during scheduled failover drills, and (4) a documented drill runplan and pass/fail criteria for scheduled active->passive promotion rehearsals.
acceptance_criteria: A fuzz-testing harness exists that can run N=100 randomized snapshot mutation tests and logs deterministic failure signatures
Progressive-restore flow supports staged restore points (metadata-only, index rebuild, KV apply) with validation checks between stages
Restore safety-net can abort and roll-forward to last known-good snapshot without manual intervention in >=90% of simulated corruptions
SLO gate integration: drills that perform partial restores will automatically trip circuit breakers to isolate traffic and surface a single failover metric in the console
Runbook and drill checklist published in Confluence with links to test artifacts and tooling; at least one scheduled drill completed with telemetry annotated
checklist: Design fuzz mutation model and failure taxonomy
Implement snapshot mutator and deterministic seed mode
Add progressive-restore orchestration with stage-level assertions
Integrate restore safety-net with circuit-breaker and load-shedding hooks
Create telemetry assertions and dashboards for drill visibility
Author runbook and schedule inaugural drill with SRE ops team
steps: 1) Kickoff with SRE/Storage/Runtime leads to align on acceptable failure modes (2026-02-22)
2) Prototype snapshot mutator that flips metadata checksums, truncates last segment, and injects stale KV revisions
3) Build deterministic test runner (seeded runs) — produce reproducible failing snapshot artifact for investigatory play
4) Implement progressive-restore controller with three stages and per-stage validators: meta-check, index-rebuild-check, KV-consistency-check

5) Wire safety-net to fallback: if KV-consistency-check fails, controller marks snapshot bad and advances to next candidate or halts with human alert; integrate circuit-breaker to divert traffic and enable emergency hot-standby
6) Add telemetry events and tags: restore.attempt, restore.stage, restore.validation.*, drill.id, circuitbreaker.trip, load_shed.action
7) Run staged test matrix (simple corruption -> complex corruption) and record success/failure rates; capture posters and forensic snapshots
8) Publish runbook and schedule first controlled drill in lower-tier region with ops present; capture lessons and iterate
decisions: Use a seeded fuzzing approach (deterministic reproduction) rather than pure random for initial runs to support forensics — agreed 2026-02-25
Adopt progressive-restore model (meta -> index -> kv) to reduce blast radius and allow SLO gating between stages
Circuit-breaker integration will be 'read-only isolation' during drills (divert writes) to avoid data divergence — finalized 2026-03-02
Safety-net behavior: prefer automated abort then promote next candidate snapshot rather than immediate manual rollback to minimize human-in-the-loop during drills
